content.value_statement: Pull request descriptions often miss context and review conventions. This skill guides branch checks, description writing, GitHub CLI creation, and reviewer requests.
actual_capabilities: Checks branch status and commit history before opening a pull request.
Reviews the branch diff against main to understand the change scope.
Drafts concise PR descriptions with motivation, context, and issue references.
Creates pull requests with GitHub CLI when gh is authenticated.
Adds individual or team reviewers through GitHub CLI when names are provided.
Formats PR titles and issue references using Sentry-style conventions.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI to be installed, authenticated, and available in the shell.
Assumes main is the comparison branch unless the user provides another base.
Does not run tests or verify continuous integration results by itself.
Creates or edits remote GitHub pull requests when the workflow is executed.

use_cases.title: Open a feature pull request
use_cases.description: Prepare a clear feature PR with context, motivation, and a Sentry-style title.

use_cases.title: Package a bug fix for review
use_cases.description: Turn a focused fix branch into a reviewer-ready PR with issue references.

use_cases.title: Standardize team PR descriptions
use_cases.description: Help contributors follow a consistent structure before requesting review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic pull request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a focused branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-pr to check my current branch, draft a Sentry-style title and description, then create the pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Draft before publishing
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare review text without remote changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-pr to inspect my commits and diff, then prepare the PR title and body only. Do not create the pull request yet.

prompt_templates.title: Create with reviewers
prompt_templates.scenario: Open a PR and assign known reviewers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-pr to create a PR for this branch and request reviewers alice and bob after showing me the title and body.

prompt_templates.title: Review a complex branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preparation for larger or mixed changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use create-pr to compare this branch with main, identify unrelated changes, propose a title, draft the body, and recommend reviewers.

output_examples.input: Create a PR for my current feature branch.
output_examples.output: The skill checks branch status, reviews commits and diff, drafts a feature-focused title, writes context for reviewers, and opens the PR.

output_examples.input: Draft a PR description without publishing it.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a concise title and body that explain what changed, why it changed, and which issue it relates to.

output_examples.input: Open this bug fix PR and add two reviewers.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a bug fix PR, then uses GitHub CLI to request the specified reviewers.

best_practices: Commit all intended changes before running the skill.
Review the proposed title and body before allowing remote GitHub changes.
Keep each PR focused on one feature, fix, or refactor.
anti_patterns: Do not bundle unrelated changes into one pull request.
Do not use the skill when GitHub CLI is not authenticated.
Do not replace reviewer context with a diff summary only.

faq.question: Does this skill create the pull request for me?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use GitHub CLI to create a pull request when gh is installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can I ask for a draft only?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask it to draft the title and body without creating the pull request.

faq.question: Which branch does it compare against?
faq.answer: The instructions use main as the default comparison branch.

faq.question: Does it run tests before creating a PR?
faq.answer: No. It checks branch state and diffs, but it does not run tests unless separately requested.

faq.question: Can it add reviewers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can request individual users or GitHub teams when reviewer names are provided.

faq.question: Is it specific to Sentry projects?
faq.answer: It follows Sentry conventions, but the general PR workflow can fit similar GitHub repositories.
